skills.name: test-your-prediction
skills.description: Use when a user has a specific low-stakes feared prediction that can be checked safely. Turn it into one observable prediction, one safe observation, and one result without dismissing genuine danger.

skills.name: problem-or-worry
skills.description: Use when a user is looping on a concern and needs to separate an actionable present problem from a future-focused what-if. Produce one practical next action or a bounded review point.

skills.name: spot-safety-behavior
skills.description: Use only in objectively low-risk situations to identify an extra reassurance, checking, or protective behavior that may block learning. Never remove a genuine safety measure.

skills.name: park-and-return
skills.description: Use when a non-urgent worry keeps interrupting the current task. Capture it once, choose a realistic review time, and return attention without requiring the worry to disappear.

skills.name: reflection-or-replay
skills.description: Use when a user keeps replaying an event after the main facts and usable lesson are already known. Test whether another round is producing new information, a decision, or an action.

skills.name: one-less-check
skills.description: Use only in ordinary objectively low-risk situations when a user is doing a clearly non-essential extra check or reassurance request. Skip one extra check and observe uncertainty without replacing it.

skills.name: smallest-approach-step
skills.description: Use when a user is avoiding a genuinely safe task and can define a much smaller first approach step. Shrink the task until one observable part can be done now.

skills.name: good-enough-contract
skills.description: Use when discretionary work keeps expanding because the user cannot decide when it is done. Define fit-for-purpose completion criteria before another pass.

skills.name: continuum-not-verdict
skills.description: Use when a user turns a graded result into a total success/failure verdict. Rate specific dimensions on a continuum instead of making one global judgment.

skills.name: behavior-not-identity
skills.description: Use when a user turns one behavior, choice, or skill gap into a global identity label. Translate the label into a specific reviewable description while preserving responsibility.

skills.name: same-standard-check
skills.description: Use when a user may be applying a harsher rule to themselves than to another person in genuinely similar circumstances. Compare the two standards and explain any real responsibility difference.

skills.name: invisible-fence-metaphor
skills.description: Use as a memory aid when an old learned rule may still constrain a clearly safe situation even though the original condition has changed. Ask whether the fence is actually gone before discussing any step forward.

skills.name: storm-that-never-came
skills.description: Use as a memory aid for prediction uncertainty when repeated low-risk forecasts are being treated as certainty. Preserve genuine-danger exceptions and never use the metaphor to dismiss real warning signs.

skills.name: slow-flame-metaphor
skills.description: Use as a memory aid when a safe change feels too large and the user is discounting small repeatable steps. Connect the image to one smallest approach step without promising a big outcome.

skills.name: skater-who-fell
skills.description: Use as a memory aid when one ordinary mistake is being treated as proof of permanent inability. Separate a single outcome from a learning process while preserving accountability and real skill limits.
